[[Klobjarne Geirr]] is a [[Legendary weapon|legendary]] [[spear]] with six [[skin|cosmetic styles]]. All six styles are unlocked as skins upon binding '''Klobjarne Geirr''' to the player's account. Each of the six styles of the spear represent the [[Southward Claw]] and their five closest allies from an ancient kodan tale.

== Lore ==
{{Legendary unlock text|As [[The Dragonstorm|the storm]] raged outside, [[Southward Claw|the Claw]] looked over his people. [[Kodan|Bearkin]] were huddled together for warmth—their bellies rumbled, and worry laced their eyes. But the wind was too fierce and the falling snow too thick to hunt. He looked at shivering cubs and made his choice: the Claw would lead them south, away from danger. He could wait for [[Waiting Sorrow|her]] no longer.}}

== Graphics ==
[[Klobjarne Geirr]] is a [[Lowland Kodan|lowland]] [[kodan]] theme spear imbued with a ghostly-spirit aura. The weapon visually evolves based on the skill being used, similar to how the [[Exordium]] changes shapes, each type of skill uses a different ghostly spearhead from behind the user.

;Draw/Stow effects
* When drawing, the spear glows intensely with the bluish-ghostly aura while the other five spear styles materialize as translucent, ghostly forms that float behind the user.
* When drawn, the spear pulses with an initial bluish-ghostly aura, followed by the orangish shiny light emitted by the bronze inscription on the spearhead. 
* When stowing, the ghostly spearheads merge back into the main weapon in a spiraling motion, leaving a faint wisp of spectral energy behind.
* When stowed, the orangish shiny light continues to emit from the bronze inscription on the spearhead, while the bluish ghostly aura ceases pulsing.

;Footfalls
* User leaves behinds swirls of mist. 

;Killing blow animation
* Enemies killed by a [[critical hit]] will trigger a visual effect: a large, translucent version of the current Klobjarne skin appears, impaling the enemy, followed by the other five spearheads materializing around the spear, each delivering a secondary impaling strike.

;Skill effects
* During melee chain attacks, the spearhead will swap between three set spears from behind your back with the translucent spirit aura.
* Projectile attacks will throw a matching visual for user choice of spear, as well as all of the ghost spear heads as a chasing wave.
* Skill effects are tied to the spirit spearhead from the arsenal positioned behind the user's back. If using a skin variant that: not Gierr, Gierr will take the position of that skin in the arsenal.
** The arsenal order behind the user's back follows a fixed arrangement from left to right: ''Hler, Kesja, Darr, Frakka, Atgeir''. The '''Klobjarne Geirr''': the only spearhead whose position changes.
** For example, if changing the skin from '''''Geirr''''' to '''''Frakka''''', '''''Geirr''''' will occupy the '''''Frakka''''' position, while the other skins maintain their original positions.

== Notes ==
* The default skin is {{item icon|Klobjarne Geirr}}. Upon adding the weapon to the [[Legendary Armory]], the skins {{item icon|Klobjarne Atgeir}}, {{item icon|Klobjarne Darr}}, {{item icon|Klobjarne Kesja}}, {{item icon|Klobjarne Frakka}}, and {{item icon|Klobjarne Hler}} are all unlocked as well.
* The floating spears behind the user will be the other unlocked skins of the [[Klobjarne Geirr]] not currently being used. Changing to another of the [[Klobjarne Geirr]] skins will change floating spear set.
{{bug|When equipped as an underwater weapon or when Klobjarne Geirr is the inactive weapon, the killing blow animation can still trigger.}}

== Trivia ==
* Klobjarne was released with the first content update for ''[[Guild Wars 2: Janthir Wilds]]'', [[Godspawn]].<ref name="Wrapping Up 2024">[https://www.guildwars2.com/en/news/studio-update-wrapping-up-2024/ Studio Update: Wrapping Up 2024], GuildWars2.com</ref>
* The name Klobjarne is most likely derived from Old Norse [[wiktionary:kló#Old Norse|''kló'']] and [[wiktionary:bjǫrn|''bjǫrn'']], which mean "claw" and "bear", respectively.
* Its variant names generally refer to different spears or polearm weapons:
** ''Geirr'' is Old Norse for "spear".<ref>[https://www.perseus.tufts.edu/hopper/text?doc=Perseus:text:2003.02.0002:entry=geirr "geirr"], Zoega's Old Icelandic dictionary</ref>
** ''Atgeir'' and ''kesja'' refer to a glaive or halberd. ''Atgeir'' is a derivative of ''geirr'' above, and ''kesja'' is a loanword from the Proto-Celtic ''gaisos'' / Celtic-Latin ''gaesum'' for "javelin".<ref>[[wikipedia:Viking halberd|"Viking halberd"]], Wikipedia</ref><ref>[http://www.germanic-lexicon-project.org/cgi-bin/gmc_search_v3?cmd=formquery2&query=kesja&startrow=1 "kesja"], Germanic Lexicon Project</ref>
** [[wiktionary:darr#Old Norse|''Darr'']] loosely means "javelin", sharing the same root with the word "dart".
** [[wiktionary:frakka|''Frakka'']] refers to a spear or lance. This word is where the Frank people derive their name from.
** Hler, shaped like a trident, is the only one that does not directly refer to a polearm weapon. ''Hlér'' is the Old Norse name for the sea.<ref>[[wikipedia:Ægir|"Ægir"]] (also anglicized as Hlér), Wikipedia</ref>
